orientation_note: The camera faces the machine's FRONT (waveform-paper / platen) face and sees ONE side face at the image-left; the near rocker/amplitude-bar fan protrudes on that image-left side. Perspective is unambiguous: both the base's top-front and bottom-front edges rise toward image-right and the front face is taller (nearer) at image-left, so the front face recedes to the image-right and the NEAREST base corner is at image-left (~300,2642). This reads as a FRONT-LEFT three-quarter view, which conflicts with the 'front-right' first-pass hint. Corner labels here assume the standard non-mirrored orientation: image-left = machine-LEFT (drive gear/crank on the machine's right, appearing at image-right on the far/receding side). If the team's ground-truth convention is that this image is machine-front-RIGHT (machine's right side toward camera), swap every left<->right in the corner names; the pixel coordinates are unaffected.
